_comment: Lore quest chains of the six legendary Spirlings (scripts/core/LegendQuests.gd, data/legend_quests.json). Guide -> inscription + witness -> back to the guide -> Trust betrayal 'lq_<legend>'.

lines: Sexton Ambrel: The clapper! And you read the wall, I can see it on your face. Wonderful.
Sexton Ambrel: Hand it over and I will see the bell to its rest. You have my word. It is worth a great deal. By the pound.
Sexton Ambrel smiles. It is the smile of a man adding up a bill.
Sexton Ambrel: The note in Lanternwell, the clapper from Brennet in Mossmere Grotto. A bell will not wait forever. Neither will my buyer. My choir, I mean.
Sexton Ambrel: You are the one who quieted the Hush? Splendid. I have a bell problem.
Sexton Ambrel: The old bell in the Bellstone Ruins rings with no one on the rope. It is grieving, poor thing.
Sexton Ambrel: The founders cut its true note into the east wall of Lanternwell. Old Brennet in Mossmere Grotto kept its clapper.
Sexton Ambrel: Bring me the clapper and I will ring it gently to rest. I have rested a great many bells.
Marks are cut deep into the east wall, under a coat of moss.
"Here we cast the Bellstone bell. Rung with its own clapper it sleeps, or it cracks."
Below, in a newer hand: "Bronze fetches eleven coins a pound. - A."
Old Brennet: Ambrel sent you? Of course he did. He sends everyone, sooner or later.
Old Brennet: Here, the clapper. I kept it from him for thirty years. My back gave out before my stubbornness did.
Old Brennet: Three bells in this valley went quiet after he rested them. Then a foundry in Thornridge got very rich.
Old Brennet: Whatever he promises, keep the clapper in your own pocket. Free advice. The only kind I can afford.
You know the old story and you have the clapper. Back to Sexton Ambrel in Gloamwood.
Sexton Ambrel: You kept it. Brennet got to you, the old crow.
Sexton Ambrel: Do you know what a cracked bell is worth? Nothing. A sleeping one sells by the ton.
He runs off into the trees, still shouting prices. Far off in the ruins, the bell gives one soft, grateful note.
Old Brennet tucked a Kin Charm into the clapper's cloth for you.
Sexton Ambrel: Thank you. Truly. You have no idea how hard it is to find an honest fool.
He strikes the clapper on a stone. Far off in the ruins, the bell screams, and the sound cracks the air.
Sexton Ambrel: Now it sleeps and I sell. Unless you would like to argue about it?
Sexton Ambrel: Keep your bell, then. It is cracked now anyway. Damaged goods.
He drops the clapper and flees. In the ruins the bell still rings, but its note is sore and wary.
The sexton who sold bells
Sexton Ambrel rested three bells and sold their bronze. He tried the same with Hallowmur, the living bell.
Archivist Quell: The quill! Gently. That is a priceless artefact and also my retirement plan.
Archivist Quell: Give it here and I will make the drake's book whole again.
Archivist Quell licks the tip of his pen.
Archivist Quell: The words in the Shatterfloor Mine, the quill from Idra on the Echo Path. History waits for no one. Except me.
Archivist Quell: Ah, a Wayfarer who reads. Rare. Most of you only read signposts, and badly.
Archivist Quell: An ink drake sleeps in the Wrenhollow Library. Scriptorax. It writes down every true road in Veydal.
Archivist Quell: Its first words are on the wall of the Shatterfloor Mine. Copyist Idra on the Echo Path holds its last quill.
Archivist Quell: Bring me the quill. I will correct a few small mistakes in its book. For the public good.
Faint lines of old ink still cling to the rock, as if someone drew a map straight onto the mine wall.
"The first map of Veydal was drawn here. Its ink woke and flew. Whoever holds its quill can make it write lies as truth."
Someone added a route in fresh ink. It runs from the Saltmarsh past every toll post. Neat work. Very illegal.
Copyist Idra: Quell? He fired me for copying a map correctly. Said it lacked vision.
Copyist Idra: Take the quill. He wants the drake to write his smugglers' road into the true map. Then no Warden ever checks it.
Copyist Idra: Hand it to him and the drake carries his lie forever. Keep it. Or don't. I'm a copyist, I only repeat things.
You know the old story and you have the quill. Back to Archivist Quell in Quillbrook.
Archivist Quell: Idra. Of course. I should have fired her harder.
Archivist Quell: Keep your quill. I will find another way to write myself rich.
He sweeps out with an armful of forged maps. Far off in the library, pages rustle as if something is laughing.
Copyist Idra slipped a Kin Charm into the quill's case for you.
Archivist Quell: Splendid. And now, a small correction.
He writes a line in the air. Far off in the Wrenhollow Library, a page tears itself out of a book with a shriek of ink.
Archivist Quell: There. The drake will remember my road as true. Unless you would like to edit me?
Archivist Quell: Fine! Footnote me, then. The drake has tasted my ink already.
He drops the quill and runs. In the library the drake wakes angry, and it does not trust a hand that holds a pen.
The archivist's road
Archivist Quell tried to write a smugglers' road into the drake's true map of Veydal.
Kitewright Dessa: The spool! Oh, look at that knot. Give it here, love.
Kitewright Dessa: One new string and it's tied down safe forever. At peace, I mean.
Kitewright Dessa winds a hook onto the end of her line.
Kitewright Dessa: Rain Rift wall, then Tibbet in Woadfen. The wind won't hold still for us forever.
Kitewright Dessa: You stood at the edge of the Wide Rift and kept your lunch down? Then you're my kind of Wayfarer.
Kitewright Dessa: Above the Rift lives Zephyrel. Four wings, never lands. Born from a kite whose string snapped.
Kitewright Dessa: The tale of that kite is cut into the Rain Rift wall. A dyer's boy in Woadfen, Tibbet, found the old spool.
Kitewright Dessa: Bring me the spool. I'll tie it a new string so it can finally rest.
A picture is scratched into the rock: a child, a kite, and a string that goes up and never comes down.
"The wind kept my kite. Whoever ties its old string again holds it like a leash."
Under it, a tally of little kites, each one crossed out. Someone has been counting catches.
Tibbet: Dessa? She buys every kite string I find. Pays well too. Then the birds over the fen go missing.
Tibbet: Here's the spool. She hooks them on her strings and sells them to a collector in Madderby. Says they flew away.
Tibbet: Don't give it to her, all right? My mum says never trust someone who sells sky by the yard.
You know the old story and you have the spool. Back to Kitewright Dessa in Greyreach.
Kitewright Dessa: The dyer's brat. Should have paid him more.
Kitewright Dessa: Keep it, then! Plenty of things in the sky that can't say no.
She stalks off down the mountain. High above the Wide Rift, the wind starts again, light and easy.
Tibbet tied a Kin Charm to the spool for you.
Kitewright Dessa: Ta, love. And now, the leash.
She casts a hooked line into the wind. Over the Wide Rift, something with four wings is jerked out of the air.
Kitewright Dessa: Sold before it lands. Unless you've got a bid of your own?
Kitewright Dessa: All right, all right! Cut it loose. It's ruined for the collector anyway.
The hook comes free. Above the Rift, Zephyrel shakes off the line, and now it watches every hand on the ground.
The kitewright's hooks
Kitewright Dessa hooked Spirlings out of the sky and sold them. She wanted Zephyrel next.
Stonecutter Dorran: That's the chisel, all right. Feel the weight of it.
Stonecutter Dorran: Hand it over. One clean rune and that stone won't trouble anyone ever again.
Stonecutter Dorran already has a sketch of a headstone in his apron pocket.
Stonecutter Dorran: Glass Rift wall, then Moll in Gravers' Hall. Stone is patient. I'm not.
Stonecutter Dorran: You sealed the Kiln Rift? Good. Now there's a stone standing in there that shouldn't be.
Stonecutter Dorran: Monolurk, they call it. A rune stone that got up and walked. Bad for business. Stones are meant to stay put.
Stonecutter Dorran: Its runes are copied on the wall of the Glass Rift. Gravedigger Moll in Gravers' Hall has its rune chisel.
Stonecutter Dorran: Bring me the chisel. I'll cut it a kinder rune and it'll sleep sound.
Rows of runes run along the wall, half melted by old heat.
"The stone guards the kiln. Its chisel cut its runes. A new rune from that chisel is its last word."
Someone scratched a price list below. Headstone, small. Headstone, large. Headstone, walking.
Gravedigger Moll: Dorran? He's cut half the stones in my yard. Never asks where the stone came from.
Gravedigger Moll: Here's the chisel. A new rune from it won't make the stone sleep. It makes it a headstone. Still. Forever.
Gravedigger Moll: He'd sell a gravestone that used to be alive. Folk pay double for a story. Keep the chisel, dear.
You know the old story and you have the chisel. Back to Stonecutter Dorran on the Saltglass Flats.
Stonecutter Dorran: Moll's been talking. The dead are quieter than her.
Stonecutter Dorran: Keep it. A rock's a rock. I'll find one that hasn't got friends.
He stomps off over the flats. Deep in the Kiln Rift, a stone lets out a long breath, like a sigh of relief.
Gravedigger Moll wrapped a Kin Charm around the chisel's handle for you.
Stonecutter Dorran: Lovely. Now, the inscription. Here lies a rock. It wouldn't sit still.
He cuts a rune into a slab of glass. Far off in the Kiln Rift, Monolurk groans as its runes go dark one by one.
Stonecutter Dorran: Unless you'd like to be the second headstone today?
Stonecutter Dorran: Have it your way! Half the rune is cut already. It'll never stand quite straight again.
He drops the chisel and runs. In the Kiln Rift, Monolurk stands, cracked and wary of any tool in a hand.
The stonecutter's headstone
Stonecutter Dorran wanted to cut a last rune into Monolurk and sell it as a headstone that used to walk.
Lamplighter Corla: The dark wick! That's the real one. Give it here before it gets dark.
Lamplighter Corla: One flame and the moth is mine. Safe, I mean. Safe with me.
Lamplighter Corla's lamp is already open, waiting for something to put inside.
Lamplighter Corla: Soot Vaults wall, then Kesk in Cinderfold. The lamps won't fix themselves. Well, they will. That's the problem.
Lamplighter Corla: Every lamp in Ashmere has flickered since you sealed the Shade Rift. Thanks for that.
Lamplighter Corla: It's Vorlucent, the eclipse moth. It eats light, and my wages are paid in light.
Lamplighter Corla: The miners drew its story in the Soot Vaults. Coal Runner Kesk in Cinderfold has its dark wick.
Lamplighter Corla: Bring me the wick. I'll light it and lure the moth somewhere it can rest. Far from my lamps.
Soot has been wiped off the wall in a wide circle. Under it is a moth with two dark rings on its wings.
"Light the dark wick and the moth comes. Hold the flame and it cannot leave. Its wing dust sends a whole town to sleep."
Below it someone has written: Sleeping towns do not lock their doors.
Coal Runner Kesk: Corla? Lovely woman. Her lamps go dark the same nights the clan houses rob someone.
Coal Runner Kesk: Here's the wick. She'll trap the moth in a lamp and shake its dust off for the clans. A whole town asleep, doors open.
Coal Runner Kesk: You didn't get this from me. I've got a family. Well, a cousin who owes me money. Same thing.
You know the old story and you have the dark wick. Back to Lamplighter Corla at Ashmere Station.
Lamplighter Corla: Kesk. That coal-faced little snitch.
Lamplighter Corla: Keep your wick! The clans will just have to rob towns while they're awake. How tiring for everyone.
She blows out her lamp and slips into the crowd. In the Shade Rift, two dark rings open slowly, unafraid.
Coal Runner Kesk wrapped a Kin Charm in the wick's paper for you.
Lamplighter Corla: Thank you, sweet. Now let's watch it dance.
She lights the wick. The station lamps flare, and far off in the Shade Rift a great moth is dragged toward a flame it cannot leave.
Lamplighter Corla: My clients pay by the pinch. Shall I put you to sleep first?
Lamplighter Corla: Fine, let it go! Half the dust is shaken off anyway.
The flame goes out. In the Shade Rift, Vorlucent shudders free, and it will not come near a lit hand again in a hurry.
The lamplighter's dust
Lamplighter Corla sold moth dust to the clans to put towns to sleep before a robbery. She tried to trap Vorlucent for it.
Pilgrim Sevrin: The ember glass. Bless you. Give it here, quickly. The light is wasted on the free.
Pilgrim Sevrin: With this, no one will ever be lost without me again.
Pilgrim Sevrin is already counting coins on his fingers.
Pilgrim Sevrin: Oasis Rift wall, then Obed in the Tower Rift. The dunes are patient. Pilgrims are not.
Pilgrim Sevrin: Travellers lost in the dunes follow a light home. A deer with a lantern heart. Lumivane.
Pilgrim Sevrin: I guide pilgrims too. For a small fee. Smaller than dying of thirst, anyway.
Pilgrim Sevrin: Its story is carved in the Oasis Rift. Hermit Obed in the Tower Rift keeps its ember glass.
Pilgrim Sevrin: Bring me the glass. With it I can send the deer to every lost soul at once.
Pictures are carved into the rock: a line of travellers, a desert, a small light leading them home.
"The first lantern lives in the deer. Shut its ember in glass and its light shines for one hand only."
Someone scratched a price beside the travellers. Then a higher price. Then a much higher one.
Hermit Obed: Sevrin. He leads pilgrims into the dunes, then sells them the way out. Water costs extra.
Hermit Obed: Here is the ember glass. Shut the deer's light in it and only Sevrin can show the way. Then everyone lost pays him.
Hermit Obed: I came out here to get away from people like him. Then they built a pilgrim road past my door. Keep the glass.
You know the old story and you have the ember glass. Back to Pilgrim Sevrin in Ochrewell.
Pilgrim Sevrin: The hermit. He never did like competition.
Pilgrim Sevrin: Keep it! The desert is big. Someone will always need me.
He hurries off with his water skins. On the crown of the Sun Rift, a soft light glows a little brighter.
Hermit Obed hid a Kin Charm in the glass's pouch for you.
Pilgrim Sevrin: Thank you, friend. Now the light belongs to whoever holds the glass.
He raises the glass toward the Sun Rift. Far off, the deer's lantern dims as its light is pulled into his hand.
Pilgrim Sevrin: The first lost soul I charge is you. Pay up, or fight?
Pilgrim Sevrin: Take the cursed thing! Half the light is out of it anyway.
The glass cracks open. At the Sun Rift, Lumivane's lantern flickers back, but now it shies from any hand held out to it.
The pilgrim's toll
Pilgrim Sevrin led pilgrims into the dunes and sold them the way out. He wanted to shut Lumivane's light in glass.
